strings.Buyers go down the list. For the item yo: Buyers go down the list. For the item you have open and every item you have listed, a buyer turns up every 15 seconds to a minute and takes the cheapest single offer (not packs or barters) if the price is one people pay. Your offer sells when the buyers get to it, so cheaper offers go first. Each buyer takes one or two, or a round lot of ammo, and buyers come less often after each sale, so a pile sells a bit at a time. A bought offer is replaced by a new seller a few minutes later. The game's average price when you list is Better Flea's normal price, so listing at the average is fair.

strings.Every base-game item starts from Better: Every base-game item starts from Better Flea's own price instead of SPT's: one fixed price per item, worked out from real PvP and PvE flea prices and trader prices. Think of it as a more reliable handbook. It doesn't move by itself; levels, multipliers, demand, drift and the Wipe Cycle still apply on top. While it's on, live prices aren't used.
strings.Traders pay you what they do in the live: Traders pay you what they do in the live game. Each trader takes its live cut of an item's base price: Therapist pays 51% instead of SPT's 63%, Prapor 40% instead of 50%, Fence 24% instead of 40%. Players see the new prices after logging in again. A trader another mod has changed (SVM's Trader markup, say) keeps that mod's price.
strings.The base-game items WTT ContentBackport: The base-game items WTT ContentBackport adds (newer items SPT doesn't have yet) get Better Flea's price too, about 675 of them. Off: they keep the price ContentBackport gives them. Does nothing without ContentBackport.
strings.Items the real game doesn't have get a p: Items the real game doesn't have get a price on the same scale, worked out from similar base-game items. Real-game items that a mod adds back (content backports) get Better Flea's price.
strings.Every item starts from its real flea pri: Every item starts from its real flea price: the 24 hour average on tarkov.dev. All of Better Flea's pricing goes on top. Prices are saved, so if tarkov.dev is down the last ones are used.
strings.Items the real game doesn't have get a p: Items the real game doesn't have get a price on the live scale, worked out from similar base-game items. Real-game items that a mod adds back (content backports) are not counted as modded: they get their real price, or keep their own if the real flea doesn't sell them.
strings.Fetch new prices this long after the las: Fetch new prices this long after the last fetch. Goes by the clock, so restarts don't matter.
strings.Prices follow how far into the wipe the: Prices follow how far into the wipe the players online are, shaped by how real flea prices moved through a wipe. Early on, hideout and quest items are dear and everything is scarce. Late on, the best guns, ammo, armour and stims are dear, and early-wipe items are cheap. The Live progression flea style turns it on.

strings.Let modded parts their mod marks as not: Let modded parts their mod marks as not sellable on the flea go on other sellers' guns. Some mods mark parts a gun needs (WTT's F2000 top rail: no rail, no scope), so this gives those guns more builds. Off: they never go on a build, like base-game flea-banned parts. They still can't be listed on their own either way.
strings.Turn a mod's attachments off on gun buil: Turn a mod's attachments off on gun builds. They're still used where a gun needs a part and nothing else fits, so a mod that depends on another (JSOC needs Epic's All in One) still gets built. Its own guns can still be listed as they come.

strings.Not recommended, and there's little reas: Not recommended, and there's little reason to use it: it's only here for anyone who preferred how 2.5.1 felt. On: an offer over normal goes by 2.5.1's percent rule instead of the room above. Every item gets the same room as a share of its price, with no rouble room, no extra room for gear and no less room on dear items, so overpricing hardly matters: a 12 hour offer 40% over still sells most of the time. Off is the default and the fairer rule.
strings.The keys this goes for. As it ships: eve: The keys this goes for. As it ships: every key with no use in the game, the ten Health Resort room keys on Shoreline, the Gas station, Store, Weapon and Weather station safe keys, the Folding car, VAZ and Yotota car keys, both Pumping station keys, the Pinewood hotel room 206 key, the Unity Credit Bank archive room key, the RB-PP key and the Missam forklift key. Add any other key a map mod leaves without a use.
strings.Keys that open nothing in the game: no l: Keys that open nothing in the game: no lock on any map takes them and no quest needs them (the door, safe or car is always open, or gone). Nobody can have used one, so they're always listed new, and with no use they're worth little, never under what a trader pays. Turn it off for their usual price.
strings.On: the Lookup tab shows exactly how oft: On: the Lookup tab shows exactly how often and how fast an offer sells at each price, for every item and every player's offer. A player who can see that prices right up to the limit, so it's off by default. Off: each player's offer only says roughly how it's priced (underpriced, priced well, a bit dear, overpriced), and Item lookup doesn't show the odds.
